title: cylinder
body:
## cylinder

Creates a closed, capped polygonal cylinder about the local Z axis with Blender's bmesh cone generator using the same radius at both ends; depth is the full height, centred on centre. The ends are single n-gon caps. Use cone for tapered sections and lathe for arbitrary axisymmetric profiles.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The axis is always local Z; use transform rotation to align it with another axis.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `cylinder`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Radius of both circular ends; the polygon vertices lie on this circle, so the faceted side is slightly inside it. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `1` |
| `depth` | Full length of the cylinder along local Z; the ends sit at -depth/2 and +depth/2 relative to centre. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `2` |
| `segments` | Number of vertices around each end circle, and so the number of side faces. Increase it for smooth silhouettes in close-up renders; combine a modest count with smoothShading to hide facets cheaply. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `32` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the middle of the cylinder's axis. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated cylinder is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
